records.label: Two Kentucky and Indiana families

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

records.segregation: Enzyme variant detectable in hematologically normal heterozygotes
quotes: Eight children (5 living, 3 deceased) with severe hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency have been observed in two Kentucky and Indiana families. All affected children were severely anemic in early life.
Three deaths occurred in young patients who did not receive adequate transfusions of blood or whose parents refused to permit splenectomy.
Growth and development have been surprisingly normal and no patient has died of infection.

phenotypes.text: marked thermal instability of erythrocyte GPI
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

phenotypes.text: normal leukocyte and plasma GPI activity

quotes: Studies of a Mexican kindred present evidence for a unique phenotype of erythrocyte glucosephosphate isomerase, GPI Valle Hermoso.

The proband was apparently the homozygous recipient of a mutant autosomal allele governing production of an isozyme characterized by decreased activity, marked thermal instability, normal kinetics and pH optimum, and normal starch gel electrophoretic patterns.
Unlike previously known cases, leukocyte and plasma GPI activities were unimpaired.

records.label: Proband (GPI deficiency type Nijmegen)

phenotypes.text: infection-triggered increase in hemolysis requiring blood transfusions

variants.as_reported: two different GPI deficient alleles (double heterozygous state)

records.segregation: One deficient allele each present in the parents and grandparents, who showed no sign of hemolysis
quotes: The clinical course and the biochemical findings are reported from a patient suffering from glucosephosphate isomerase (G.P.I EC 5.3.1.9) deficiency type Nijmegen. This disorder decleares itself as a non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia, presenting in the neonatal period.
However, trivial infections could often trigger an increase in hemolysis requiring treatment by blood transfusions.
Enzyme studies revealed that the GPI deficiency in this patient was caused by a double heterozygous state for two different GPI deficient alleles.

Propositus was double heterozygote for a 'silent gene' inherited from the mother and an abnormal enzyme from the father.

GPI 'Paris' was characterized by a slow electrophoretic migration and, above all, a drastically altered affinity for the substrates glucose-6-phosphate (decreased) and fructose-6-phosphate (increased).

GPI 'Enfants malades' exhibited a slightly reduced electrophoretic mobility, an abnormal curve of the activity in function of pH, and an abnormal ratio of maximal velocity in the backward direction

records.label: 5-year-old Italian boy

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal erythrocyte enzyme concentration or activity

quotes: A severe hemolytic crisis was observed in a 5-year-old boy of Italian origin. Analysis of his hemolysate revealed a hemizygous deficiency of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) and a heterozygous deficiency of glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI).
Only the G6PD deficiency seems to be responsible for the hemolytic crisis.

records.label: 13-year-old German girl

phenotypes.text: recurrent hemolytic crises after febrile infections

records.segregation: Family examination indicated the patient is doubly heterozygous for the deficiency
quotes: In a 13-year-old German girl a GPI deficiency was found to be the cause of a chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with recurrent hemolytic crises. The hemolytic crises usually occurred after a feverish infection.
Only once did the patient require blood transfusion during a crisis. Examination of the family indicated that the patient is doubly heterozygous for the deficiency.

records.segregation: PGI*3 allele observed in 11 of 32 family members tested; autosomal codominant inheritance
quotes: Phosphoglucose isomerase (PGI) and 16 other biochemical genetic markers were studied in an Israeli-Arab family previously described for hereditary deficiency of adenylate kinase (AK) and glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD).
In this inbred family a rare PGI*3 allele was observed in 11 of 32 members tested, indicating an autosomal codominant inheritance.
This PGI*3 allele, designated PGI*3 (Israel), seems to be a different unstable mutation and along with AK and G6PD deficiencies seems to be associated with severe anaemia.

The neurologically affected patient (GPI Homburg) is compound heterozygous for a 59 A-->C (H20P) and a 1016 T-->C (L339P) exchange.

notes.statement: Kugler et al. (1998) suggested that GPI mutations causing incorrect folding, such as the proline insertions H20P and L339P in GPI Homburg, destroy both the catalytic (GPI) and the neurotrophic (neuroleukin) activities, which would lead to neurological dysfunction. They proposed that changes at the active site that still allow correct folding, as in GPI Calden, keep the neurotrophic properties.
quotes: Owing to the insertion of proline, the H20P and L339P mutations are likely to affect the folding and activity of the enzyme.
We propose that mutations that lead to incorrect folding destroy both catalytic (GPI) and neurotrophic (NLK) activities, thereby leading to the observed clinical symptoms (GPI Homburg).

notes.statement: Walker et al. (1993) reported DNA sequence abnormalities in human glucose 6-phosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: DNA sequence abnormalities in human glucose 6-phosphate isomerase deficiency.

notes.statement: Merkle and Pretsch (1993) described the first 2 mutations causing hereditary GPI deficiency with chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia in a nonhuman mammal, the mouse. As in humans, the hemolytic syndrome appeared only in homozygous mutants. It included a reduced erythrocyte count, lower hematocrit and hemoglobin, reticulocytosis, raised plasma bilirubin, and hepatosplenomegaly.
quotes: The first two mutations causing hereditary glucose-6-phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency associated with chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia in nonhuman mammals are described in the mouse.

As in humans, the hemolytic syndrome, which is characterized by a diminished erythrocyte number, lower hematocrit, lower hemoglobin, higher number of reticulocytes and plasma bilirubin concentration, as well as increased liver- and spleen-somatic indices, was exclusively manifested in homozygous mutants.

notes.statement: Merkle and Pretsch (1993) found no hematologic or other physiologic differences between heterozygous Gpi mutant mice and wildtype mice. Erythrocytes from homozygous mutants had increased glucose-6-phosphate, normal or decreased levels of the downstream glycolytic metabolites, and apparently reduced ATP and glycolytic rate.
quotes: In comparison with wild type, heterozygous individuals exhibited neither hematologic differences nor alterations of other physiologic parameters

homozygous mutant erythrocytes showed an increased concentration of glucose-6-phosphate and normal or decreased concentrations of glycolytic metabolites following the enzymatic block. The concentration of adenosine triphosphate and the glycolytic rate also appeared to be reduced.

notes.statement: Merkle and Pretsch (1993) found that homozygous anemic mice showed adaptations to hypoxia, including an elevated heart-somatic index. They also had markedly reduced body weight and increased lethality, both correlated with the degree of enzyme deficiency in tissues. The authors attributed these findings to a reduced glycolytic capability of the whole organism rather than to secondary effects of the erythrocyte defect.
quotes: Homozygous anemic mice showed hepatosplenomegaly and typical adaptations to hypoxia, such as an elevated heart-somatic index and, for one mutant line, an enhanced lung-somatic index.
these animals were characterized by a marked reduction of body weight and an increase of lethality both correlated with the degree of enzyme deficiency in tissues.

The latter findings were attributed to a reduced glycolytic capability of the whole organism caused by the enzyme defect in tissues, rather than representing secondary consequences of GPI deficiency in erythrocytes.

notes.statement: Shalev et al. (1993) found that the GPI variant in their patient, designated GPI Mount Scopus, showed slow electrophoretic mobility, only one of the two bands normally present, and extreme thermolability.
quotes: The biophysical characteristics of the GPI variant are slow electrophoretic mobility, presence of only one of the two bands normally present, and extreme thermolability.

notes.statement: Shalev et al. (1993) stated that, to their knowledge, theirs was the first report of GPI deficiency in a patient of Jewish descent.
quotes: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of GPI deficiency in a patient of Jewish descent

notes.statement: Shalev et al. (1993) described GPI deficiency as an unusual, autosomal recessive cause of hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia, most often manifested by chronic hemolysis that is ameliorated by splenectomy.
quotes: The disease, inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder, is most often manifested by symptoms and signs of chronic hemolysis, ameliorated by splenectomy.

notes.statement: Zanella et al. (1980) found that the variant GPI had increased affinity for fructose-6-phosphate, decreased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate, altered electrophoretic and isoelectrofocusing patterns, and a left shift of the precipitin curve, but was stable to heat, urea, guanidine-HCl, and storage, with normal pH optimum, Ki values, molecular weight, and GPI-related antigen concentration.
quotes: The defective enzyme showed increased affinity for fructose-6-phosphate (F-6-P), decreased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate (G-6-P) altered electrophoretic and isoelectrofocusing patterns, and shift to the left of the precipitin curve.
The enzyme was stable under all the conditions tested (heat, urea, guanidine-HCl, and storage).

notes.statement: Zanella et al. (1980) reported the first example of a stable mutant GPI associated with severe hemolytic anemia, noting that enzyme instability had been present in all previously reported cases.
quotes: This is the first example of the association of a stable mutant GPI with severe hemolytic anemia. Enzyme instability has been present in all previously reported cases.

notes.statement: Arnold et al. (1980) found that the deficient GPI enzyme in their patient showed altered electrophoretic mobility, pronounced thermolability, increased affinity for G6P and for the competitive inhibitor 6-PG, and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates. They designated this new variant GPI Augsburg.
quotes: The investigation of the biochemical properties of the deficient enzyme revealed an altered electrophoretic behavior, pronounced thermolability, an increased affinity for G6P, an increased affinity for the competitive inhibitor 6-PG, and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates.
The properties of the new deficient GPI indicate a new variant designated GPI Augsburg.

notes.statement: Arnold et al. (1980) found from electrophoresis after freezing and thawing the hemolysate that the genetic change in the subunit appeared to affect the process that converts the main band into the secondary bands.
quotes: Electrophoresis after freezing and thawing the hemolysate indicates that the genetic modification of the subunit involves the mechanism of transforming the main band into the secondary bands.

notes.statement: Arnold et al. (1981) reported a 5-year-old Italian boy with a severe hemolytic crisis who had hemizygous G6PD deficiency combined with heterozygous GPI deficiency. They noted that this was the fourth reported family with combined deficiency of these two enzymes, and they concluded that only the G6PD deficiency seemed to be responsible for the hemolytic crisis.
quotes: According to the literature this is the fourth family with a combined deficiency of these two enzymes located on different chromosomes. Only the G6PD deficiency seems to be responsible for the hemolytic crisis.

notes.statement: Arnold et al. (1983) found that the deficient GPI enzyme (GPI-Kaiserslautern) showed altered electrophoretic migration, pronounced thermolability, increased affinity for glucose-6-phosphate, and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates, indicating a new variant.
quotes: The investigation of the biochemical properties of the deficient enzyme revealed an altered electrophoretic migration, a pronounced thermolability, an increased affinity for G-6-P and slightly changed pH optima for both substrates.

notes.statement: Paglia et al. (1969) reported defective hexosephosphate isomerization in both erythrocytes and leukocytes in humans.
quotes: Occurrence of defective hexosephosphate isomerization in human erythrocytes and leukocytes.

notes.statement: Detter et al. (1968) reported inherited variations in human phosphohexose isomerase.
quotes: Inherited variations in human phosphohexose isomerase.

notes.statement: Baughan et al. (1968) described hereditary hemolytic anemia associated with glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency as a new enzyme defect of human erythrocytes.
quotes: Hereditary hemolytic anemia associated with glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency--a new enzyme defect of human erythrocytes.

notes.statement: Using biochemical variants in mice, Hutton (1969) showed that the hemoglobin beta-chain locus and the glucosephosphate isomerase locus were linked.
quotes: Linkage analyses using biochemical variants in mice. I. Linkage of the hemoglobin beta-chain and glucosephosphate isomerase loci.

notes.statement: Blume et al. (1972) characterized two new variants of glucose-phosphate-isomerase deficiency associated with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
quotes: Characterization of two new variants of glucose-phosphate-isomerase deficiency with hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.

notes.statement: Blume and Beutler (1972) described a screening procedure for detecting glucose-phosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: Detection of glucose-phosphate isomerase deficiency by a screening procedure.

notes.statement: Beutler et al. (1974) reported a variant of glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency, which they called GPI Elyria.
quotes: Glucosephosphate-isomerase (GPI) deficiency: GPI elyria.

notes.statement: Paglia and Valentine (1974) reviewed hereditary glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency.
quotes: Hereditary glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency. A review.

notes.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) found that splenectomy generally abolished the requirement for blood transfusion in GPI deficiency, and no patient required regular transfusion after puberty.
quotes: Splenectomy generally abolishes the requirement for blood transfusion. No patient has required regular transfusion of blood after puberty.

notes.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) concluded that the anemia was expressed as an autosomal recessive trait, although the enzyme variant could be detected in hematologically normal heterozygotes.
quotes: The anemia is expressed as an autosomal recessive trait, but the enzyme variant can be detected in hematologically normal heterozygotes.

notes.statement: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) found that the abnormal isomerase molecule was heat labile and was present in neutrophils and lymphocytes as well as in erythrocytes.
quotes: The abnormal isomerase molecule is heat labile and is contained in neutrophils and lymphocytes as well as in erythrocytes.

notes.statement: Schröter et al. (1985) described a new GPI variant, GPI Homburg. It had very low specific activity in erythrocytes, granulocytes and muscle tissue, nearly normal stability, normal kinetic properties and decreased electrophoretic mobility.
quotes: A new glucosephosphate isomerase (GPI) variant is described which is characterised by very low specific activity in erythrocytes, granulocytes and muscle tissue, nearly normal stability, normal kinetic properties and a decreased electrophoretic mobility.

notes.statement: Schröter et al. (1985) suggested that the clinical syndrome resulted from generalized GPI deficiency caused by the decreased specific activity of the variant enzyme. They proposed that increased de novo synthesis of GPI protein could not make up for this deficiency, even in cells with active protein synthesis such as granulocytes and muscle cells.
quotes: It is suggested that the clinical syndrome results from generalised GPI deficiency due to a decreased specific activity of the variant enzyme, which cannot be compensated by an increase of de-novo synthesis of GPI protein even in cells exhibiting active protein synthesis such as granulocytes and muscle cells.

notes.statement: Ravindranath et al. (1987) reported glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency as a cause of hydrops fetalis.
quotes: Glucose phosphate isomerase deficiency as a cause of hydrops fetalis.

notes.statement: Bonné-Tamir et al. (1987) found that the PGI*3(Israel) allele moved on electrophoresis like the PGI*3 allele found in Indian populations. Unlike the Indian allele, it had very low specific activity and heat stability. The authors concluded that it seemed to be a different, unstable mutation.
quotes: The electrophoretic mobility of this allele is similar to that of the PGI*3 allele found in Indian populations, but unlike the Indian allele, it has a very low specific activity and heat stability.

notes.statement: Bonné-Tamir et al. (1987) observed the rare PGI*3 allele in 11 of 32 members of an inbred Israeli-Arab family, which indicated autosomal codominant inheritance.
quotes: In this inbred family a rare PGI*3 allele was observed in 11 of 32 members tested, indicating an autosomal codominant inheritance.

notes.statement: Paglia et al. (1975) found that the GPI Valle Hermoso variant had decreased activity and marked thermal instability, but normal kinetics, normal pH optimum, and normal starch gel electrophoretic patterns. Unlike in previously known cases, leukocyte and plasma GPI activities were not impaired.
quotes: an isozyme characterized by decreased activity, marked thermal instability, normal kinetics and pH optimum, and normal starch gel electrophoretic patterns
Unlike previously known cases, leukocyte and plasma GPI activities were unimpaired.

notes.statement: Paglia et al. (1975) suggested that the structural change in GPI Valle Hermoso mainly made the enzyme unstable without greatly reducing its catalytic effectiveness. This would let cells that can keep making protein compensate. However, density-gradient fractionation of affected erythrocytes did not show age-related loss of GPI.
quotes: This suggested that the structural alteration primarily induced enzyme instability without drastically curtailing catalytic effectiveness, thereby allowing compensation by cells capable of continued protein synthesis.
Age-related losses of GPI, however, were not evident by density-gradient fractionation of affected erythrocytes.

notes.statement: Rotteveel et al. (1977) found that heterozygous carriers of one GPI-deficient allele among the proband's parents and grandparents showed no sign of hemolysis, such as shortened red-cell survival.
quotes: The presence of one of these deficient alleles in the proband's parents and grandparents, was not accompanied by any sign of hemolysis, as for instance a shortened red-cell survival.

notes.statement: Zanella et al. (1978) found that the only functional abnormality of the mutant GPI appeared to be marked instability to heat, urea, and guanidine-HCl. Incubation of normal and mutant GPI with oxidizing and reducing agents seemed to indicate that the abnormality resided in the SH groups of the mutant enzyme.
quotes: The only functional abnormality of the mutant enzyme seems to be a marked instability to heat, urea, and guanidine-HCl.
Experiments of incubation of normal GPI and the propositus's GPI with oxidizing and reducing agents seem to indicate that the abnormality resides in the SH groups of the mutant GPI.

notes.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) found that in both deficient GPI variants (GPI Paris and GPI Enfants malades) the main cause of reduced enzyme activity was molecular instability of the mutant enzyme, with nearly normal catalytic activity. GPI Paris showed slow electrophoretic migration and markedly altered substrate affinity (decreased for glucose-6-phosphate, increased for fructose-6-phosphate).
quotes: In both cases the main cause of the defect in enzyme activity was molecular instability of the mutated GPI molecules, their catalytic activity being nearly normal.

GPI 'Paris' was characterized by a slow electrophoretic migration and, above all, a drastically altered affinity for the substrates glucose-6-phosphate (decreased) and fructose-6-phosphate (increased).

notes.statement: Kahn et al. (1978) could not prove a clear relationship between the kinetic abnormalities of the mutant GPI variants and either the metabolic changes in GPI-deficient red cells or the severity of hemolysis. They suggested that impairment of the hexose monophosphate pathway might help reduce the viability of GPI-deficient red cells.
quotes: No clear relation could be proved between the kinetic abnormalities of the mutant GPI variants on the one hand and the metabolic changes of the GPI-deficient red cells and the severity of hemolysis on the other.
Finally we emphasized the possible role of the impairment of hexosemonophosphate pathway in the reduction of viability of the GPI-deficient red cells.

notes.statement: Galand et al. (1978) found that the deficient GPI enzyme in their patient (variant GPI-MYTHO) showed profoundly decreased red cell activity, normal electrophoretic phenotype, normal isoelectric point and optimum pH, molecular instability, and a clearly decreased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.
quotes: Deficient enzyme was characterized by a profoundly decreased activity in the red cells, a normal electrophoretic phenotype, normal isoelectric point, normal optimum pH, a molecular instability and a clearly decreased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.

notes.statement: Galand et al. (1978) proposed the name GPI-MYTHO for the new abnormal enzyme variant with previously undescribed characteristics.
quotes: Because this abnormal enzyme has undescribed characteristics, it responds to a new variant for which we propose the name GPI-MYTHO.

notes.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) made a prenatal diagnosis of GPI deficiency by examination of amniotic cells obtained by amniocentesis at 28 weeks in the mother's second pregnancy.
quotes: Examination of amniotic cells obtained by amniocentesis on the mother at 28 weeks in her second pregnancy led to the prenatal diagnosis of GPI deficiency.

notes.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) successfully treated a prenatally diagnosed compound heterozygous GPI-deficient infant by immediate exchange transfusion followed by blood transfusions.
quotes: was successfully treated by immediate exchange transfusion and subsequent blood transfusions.

notes.statement: Whitelaw et al. (1979) found that both healthy parents of affected children had 50% of normal red cell GPI activity and were each heterozygous for a different GPI-deficient variant allele, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance with compound heterozygosity in the affected children.
quotes: Both parents were found to have 50% of normal red cell GPI activity and qualitative tests on their red cells and white cells showed that each was heterozygous for a different GPI variant allele associated with enzyme deficiency.

notes.statement: Isacchi et al. (1979) found that the GPI Roma variant was slightly unstable to heat and had a slightly increased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.
quotes: GPI Roma was slightly unstable to heat and exhibited a slightly increased Michaelis constant for fructose-6-phosphate.

notes.statement: Isacchi et al. (1979) found a single main fast-migrating GPI form in the patient's white blood cells. In her red cells, the electrophoretic pattern also included a major band that migrated like normal GPI and an extra slow band. The authors attributed this to postsynthetic events that changed the charge of the mutant enzyme.
quotes: A single predominant fast-migrating GPI form existed in the patient's white blood cells, while the electrophoretic pattern in the red cells was composed, in addition to this 'fast band,' of a major band migrating as normal GPI and of an additional slow band.
It is shown that this phenomenon may be ascribed to postsynthetic events modifying the charge of the mutant enzyme.

notes.statement: Arnold (1979) reviewed GPI deficiency. Patients had a typical nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia, with hemolytic crises during acute infections.
quotes: The patients suffer from a typical nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia with hemolytic crises during acute infections.

notes.statement: Arnold (1979) noted that GPI deficiency is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. About half of reported patients were homozygous and the rest were double (compound) heterozygotes.
quotes: The disease is inherited as an autosomal recessive, half of the patients are homozygotic, the others are double heterozygotes.

notes.statement: Arnold (1979) found that the biochemical properties of deficient GPI enzymes varied widely, and many well-characterized enzymes had been named as separate variants. Changes in physicochemical properties outweighed kinetic abnormalities, and all defective variants were more or less unstable.
quotes: The biochemical properties of the deficient enzymes vary widely. Thus, many well characterized enzymes have been designated as different variants.
The modification of physicochemical properties surpasses kinetic aberrations. All defective variants are more or less unstable.

notes.statement: Arnold (1979) reported that GPI activity in deficient red cells fell progressively, raising the G6P concentration. After the cells aged in vitro, glycolysis was severely impaired and hemolysis followed. The metabolic block was attributed to the reduced GPI activity itself, not to inhibition of hexokinase by the high G6P.
quotes: The activity diminishes progressively, leading to a rise in G6P concentration and in red cells after aging in vitro to a dramatic impairment of glycolysis and concomittant hemolysis.
The cause of the metabolic block is the diminished GPI activity itself and not an inhibition of hexokinase by the high G6P.

notes.statement: Van Biervliet et al. (1975) found that the mutant GPI enzyme in their Dutch patient was markedly thermolabile, losing 90% of its activity after 1 hour at 45 degrees C. Its pH optimum, electrophoretic migration, Km for fructose-6-phosphate and Ki values for the competitive inhibitors 2,3-DPG and 6-PG were normal.
quotes: Characterization of the defect enzyme showed a pronounced thermolability. Heating of the enzyme at 45 degrees C showed a loss of activity of 90% after one hour.

notes.statement: Van Biervliet et al. (1975) found that this variant differed from all known GPI variants and proposed naming it GPI-Utrecht.
quotes: The variant described here differs from all known variants. Therefore we propose to give to this new variant the name of GPI-Utrecht.

notes.statement: Van Biervliet et al. (1975) described a new variant of glucosephosphate isomerase deficiency, studied its enzyme kinetics and properties, and found that genetic and electrophoretic data pointed to a double heterozygous state in the patient.
quotes: The enzyme kinetics and properties were studied. Genetic and electrophoretic data pointed to a double heterozygous state in the patient.
